summary: A hybrid superconducting qubit combines aluminum-oxide tunnel junctions with a gate-tunable InAs/Al nanowire junction in a SQUID to achieve controlled parity of Cooper pair tunneling. By tuning a single gate voltage, the device suppresses odd Josephson harmonics by up to two orders of magnitude at half-flux quantum, producing a $\cos(2\phi)$-dominated potential with a deep double well.
motivation: Conventional Josephson junctions rely on single-Cooper-pair tunneling via the $\cos(\phi)$ term, but higher harmonics $\cos(k\phi)$ corresponding to $k$-pair tunneling can improve protection in superconducting qubits. Previous work required complex multi-junction or all-hybrid architectures to achieve even-harmonic dominance; a simpler, gate-tunable approach was needed.
method: A parallel SQUID with two SIS junctions in one arm and a gate-tunable S-Sm-S nanowire junction in the other was fabricated on NbTiN. Multi-transition spectroscopy was performed at 85 gate voltages from $-7$ V to $9.8$ V, and harmonic coefficients were extracted by fitting the full circuit Hamiltonian to the reconstructed energy-phase relation.
result: The odd harmonic coefficient $c_{\mathrm{odd}}$ was reduced to 0.6 GHz from 30.9 GHz while the even coefficient $c_{\mathrm{even}}$ remained at 15–20 GHz; the ratio $|c_{\mathrm{even}}/c_{\mathrm{odd}}|$ spans nearly two orders of magnitude. At the even-dominated point ($V_g = 7.2$ V), $|c_2/c_1| = 3.47$ and the ground and excited states exhibit opposite Cooper-pair parity with suppressed parity-violating transitions.
